ENT CLINICAL NOTE

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • Sudden onset shortness of breath while sitting watching TV; began ≈1 hour prior to call.  
  • No obvious food, medication, or environmental trigger identified.

- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Shortness of breath started abruptly, has not clearly worsened but is causing anxiety and palpitations.  
  • Dry cough began the day before.  
  • Chest feels sore with deep inspiration; C-section scar also tender.

- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: Denied.  
  • Voice change/hoarseness: Denied.  
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling: Denied.  
  • Nasal/ocular symptoms: Not reported.  
  • Stridor/noisy breathing: Not reported.  
  • Dyspnea: Present (main complaint).  
  • Facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling: Denied.  
  • Ear or neck symptoms: Denied.

- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • No previous similar episodes of dyspnea.  
  • Caesarean section 4 weeks ago; took codeine post-operatively (last dose ≈1 week ago).  
  • No prior ED visits or injections for allergic or respiratory events noted.

- Allergies and current medications:
  • Allergy: Ibuprofen – reaction details not recalled.  
  • Medication: Codeine (dose/route/frequency not documented); currently not taking.

- Social context:
  • Alone at home with 4-week-old baby; partner at work.  
  • Able to self-transport to hospital.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: None mentioned (lips, tongue, face all normal).  
- Airway/breathing: Patient reports dyspnea but no stridor or audible wheeze noted during call.  
- Cardiovascular: Self-counted pulse 30 beats/15 s ≈120 bpm (tachycardic).  
- Mental status: Alert, oriented, mildly anxious.  
- Vitals and full physical examination: Not recorded.  
- Another person present: No (patient alone with infant).

Assessment:
- Acute postpartum dyspnea with tachycardia; concern for pulmonary embolism (post-C-section hypercoagulability).  
- No features of upper-airway angioedema or anaphylaxis at present.

Plan:
- Immediate actions:
  • Advised urgent hospital evaluation for suspected pulmonary embolism.  
  • Patient elected to self-transport promptly with infant and necessary supplies.  
  • Advised to withhold further codeine until assessed.

- Instructions to patient:
  • Leave for emergency department immediately; if symptoms worsen en route (increased breathlessness, chest pain, dizziness, fainting), pull over and call emergency services (999).  
  • Avoid driving if symptoms escalate; consider calling ambulance if unable to travel safely.  
  • Remain accompanied after arrival; notify staff of recent C-section and new-onset dyspnea.

- Escalation criteria/red flags:
  • Sudden worsening breathlessness, chest pain, coughing blood.  
  • Throat tightness, voice change, facial or tongue swelling, stridor.  
  • Syncope or severe dizziness.

- Follow-up:
  • Hospital team to complete work-up (e.g., D-dimer, CT pulmonary angiography) and manage as indicated.  
  • Arrange postpartum follow-up with obstetrics and primary care after discharge.  
  • Review analgesia needs; consider non-NSAID alternatives due to ibuprofen allergy.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing but expected: full vital signs (BP, RR, SpO₂, temperature), physical examination findings (lung auscultation, leg exam for DVT), detailed ibuprofen reaction, detailed medication list, availability of auto-injector not applicable but typical for allergic reviews.  
• Internal conflicts: None identified in transcript.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; minimal background noise; some portions clipped but clinical content retained.
